title: A temple prayer asks God to accept and fill his house
setting: Latter-day Saints in Kirtland, Ohio, had worked since 1833 to build the House of the Lord. On 26 March 1836, Joseph Smith met with Oliver Cowdery, Sidney Rigdon, and scribes to prepare the dedicatory prayer. The official heading says the prayer was given to them by revelation. It was printed overnight so Joseph could read it. On 27 March 1836, he read it to about 1,000 people, who accepted it by vote.
summary: The prayer thanks God and asks him to accept the house the Saints built through poverty and tribulation. It repeats the earlier command to build a house of prayer, fasting, faith, learning, glory, and order. It asks that God’s glory and presence rest there and that all who enter feel his power. It asks that servants go out armed with power and that enemies and lying reports fail. It pleads for the Saints driven from Jackson County, Missouri. It asks mercy for nations and rulers, the Constitution’s preservation, and the redemption of Jerusalem and scattered Israel. It remembers Joseph Smith, his family, the church presidents, and the whole church. It closes by asking God to accept the dedication, with the cry “Hosanna to God and the Lamb!”

contextNote.title: A house others can recognize as holy
contextNote.text: The Saints had built the house in poverty and now asked what would make it more than a building. Verse 12 asks that God’s glory and “holy presence” rest there continually. Verse 13 asks that all who cross the threshold “may feel thy power”. They would then acknowledge “that it is thy house, a place of thy holiness”. Verse 20 adds that “no unclean thing” may enter to pollute it. In this prayer, holiness is God’s presence felt by those who enter, guarded by the people’s worthiness.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 109–110 takes its title, “It Is Thy House, a Place of Thy Holiness,” from verse 13. What blessings do verses 22–23 ask for those who leave the temple?

jsp.title: Minutes and Prayer of Dedication, 27 March 1836 [D&C 109]

reviewNote: Read all 80 verses. Official heading gives the Kirtland temple dedication, 27 March 1836, and says the prayer was given by revelation. The JSP page “Prayer of Dedication, 27 March 1836 [D&C 109]” has no introduction and points to the minutes document, which was read and is cited. It gives the 26 March preparation with Cowdery, Rigdon, and scribes, overnight broadside printing, and about 1,000 attending. “Since 1833” for construction is general knowledge. independence stands for Jackson County (v. 47).
